composition.serve_who: This sheet (108-01-520-001 rev B, "Bilge & Fire System Schematic") is the master P&ID for the vessel's combined bilge and firefighting system. It shows: the Main Bilge Pump, Electric Fire Pump and Diesel Fire Pump (crash pump) all located near frame B/A (aft engine room/lazarette boundary); two Aux Bilge Pumps (Engine Room and Mast Area, Whale Gulper 320); a network of motor-actuated bilge valves at each sump/compartment; sump boxes at Lazarette, Midship, Engine Room, Mast Area, ESS Enclosure and Sail Locker; the fireline running fore-and-aft in the port sheer to hydrants/hoses fwd and aft; and the operating-modes doc (referenced by note 2) that defines Normal/Aux/Emergency-fire/Emergency-bilge lineups. Evidence: title block, BOM table (pump items 001-003, 024; valve items 016-017; sensor items 007,025), pump-data table, and the walked pipe colors (blue=main bilge, red=fireline, purple=aux bilge, dashed blue=freshwater priming).

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: This is the overall system node for the combined bilge/fire schematic; the sheet's own multi-loop, multi-pump topology (main bilge line, fireline, aux bilge line) is a system-level lineup, not any one pump's function.

functions.label: Normal Operation — Main Bilge // Main Fire
functions.what_it_does: Main Bilge Pump clears water from any of the five sumps (Lazarette, Midship, Engine Room, Mast Area, Sail Locker) via the main bilge line (blue) and discharges overboard through the anti-siphon manifold, whose breather runs into the STBD E-R vent box. In parallel, the Electric Fire Pump and Diesel Fire Pump draw seawater via a seawater strainer and pressurise the fireline (red) in the port sheer, feeding fire hose stations fore and aft and the tender-garage/lazarette sprinklers.

flow_scenarios.path: Sump (Laz/Midship/E-R/Mast/Sail Locker) -> only the NC valve(s) for the sump in use opened -> main bilge line (blue) -> Main Bilge Pump -> anti-siphon manifold -> bilge overboard (breather to STBD E-R vent box)
Seawater pickup -> seawater strainer -> Electric Fire Pump / Diesel Fire Pump -> fireline (red, port sheer) -> fwd + aft fire hydrants/hoses; tender garage & lazarette sprinklers

key_components: NC bilge valves at each sump (open only as needed)
anti-siphon manifold with breather to STBD E-R vent box
functions.dry_data: Main bilge line shown blue, fireline shown red on sheet; unnecessary engine-room/mast-sump detail hidden for clarity per drawing note.

functions.label: Auxiliary Bilge Operation — Aux pump overboard (when regulations allow)
functions.what_it_does: E-R Aux Bilge Pump and Mast Aux Bilge Pump each draw from their local sump and discharge through an oily bilge filter to the FWD deck locker drain (min 800mm above DWL), via a flex suction hose connection — an alternate discharge route from the main bilge line, used only when overboard discharge of bilge water is permitted.

flow_scenarios.path: Engine Room Sump / Mast Area Sump -> flex suction hose connection -> Aux Bilge Pump -> oily bilge filter -> FWD deck locker drain (min. 800mm above DWL) overboard

flow_scenarios.path: Engine Room Sump / Mast Area Sump -> flex suction hose connection -> Aux Bilge Pump -> oily bilge filter -> portable oil storage tank (FWD deck locker drain path shown for reference only, below DWL)

functions.label: Emergency Operation — Fire Backup (electric fire pump NOT operational)
functions.what_it_does: With the Electric Fire Pump marked NOT OPERATIONAL, the Diesel Fire Pump alone (primed from the fresh water supply per ref dwg 108-01-510-001) draws seawater via the strainer and supplies the full fireline (both fore and aft) to hydrants/hoses.

flow_scenarios.path: Seawater pickup -> seawater strainer -> Diesel Fire Pump (primed via freshwater priming line, ref dwg 108-01-510-001) -> fireline (fore+aft, port sheer) -> hydrants/hoses, tender garage/lazarette sprinklers

key_components: priming line from fresh water supply (cross-sheet)

functions.label: Emergency Operation — Bilge Backup (main bilge pump NOT operational)
functions.what_it_does: With the Main Bilge Pump marked NOT OPERATIONAL, the Diesel Fire Pump (driven via its priming line) and the STBD Genset's raw water pump take over bilge duty: sumps are drained via the same NC valve lineup logic (open only the valve(s) needed) through the anti-siphon manifold overboard, while the genset raw-water pump path discharges via the exhaust water separator (ref dwg 108-01-515-001).

flow_scenarios.path: Sump (Laz/Midship/E-R/Mast/Sail Locker) -> NC valve(s) opened as needed -> main bilge line -> Diesel Fire Pump (via priming line) -> anti-siphon manifold -> bilge overboard (breather to STBD E-R vent box)

flow_scenarios.path: Sea chest supply (ref dwg 108-01-515-003) -> STBD Genset raw water pump -> exhaust water separator (ref dwg 108-01-515-001) -> overboard

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: BOM items 016 (electric rotary actuators) + 017 (2-way ball valves DN050) — drawn as motor-actuated valves at 5 locations (lazarette, aft, E-R, mast, sail locker) controlling which sump the main bilge line draws from; normal-closed states are the operative lineup logic per operating-modes doc.

functions.label: Sump isolation valve set (5 locations)
functions.what_it_does: Each motor-actuated valve isolates its sump from the main bilge line; per operating-modes doc, these valves are normally closed and only the valve(s) for the sump actually being pumped are opened, one at a time, to prevent cross-flooding/air-locking between compartments.

flow_scenarios.path: no flow through any valve unless opened
operator/automation opens ONE valve (e.g. lazarette, aft, E-R, mast, or sail locker) -> that sump connects to main bilge line -> Main Bilge Pump or Diesel Fire Pump (backup) -> overboard
